# ResearchSense Analysis Report

**Paper:** `neural_compression_paper.pdf`
**Analysed:** 18 May 2026 — 21:58 IST
**Generated by:** ResearchSense v1.0

---

## Overall Score

| Final Score | Grade |
|---|---|
| **76 / 100** | **B — Good** |

---

## Parameter Breakdown

> Each parameter is weighted differently — total adds up to 100 marks.

---

### 1. Grammar & Language &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `12 / 15`

**Issues found:**
- 4 grammatical errors detected (subject-verb agreement, article misuse)
- Excessive use of passive voice throughout Section 3 and Section 4
- 2 run-on sentences in the Abstract

**Suggestions:**
- Run the manuscript through a grammar checker (Grammarly / LanguageTool) before resubmission
- Restructure passive constructions in the Methodology to active voice where possible
- Break run-on sentences in the Abstract into 2 shorter, clearer sentences

---

### 2. Structural Integrity &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `13 / 15`

**Issues found:**
- Discussion section is present but shorter than expected relative to Results
- Literature Review section not clearly labelled (merged into Introduction)

**Suggestions:**
- Expand the Discussion to address limitations and implications of results
- Separate Literature Review into its own clearly headed section (standard IEEE/ACM format)

---

### 3. Methodology Soundness &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `10 / 15`

**Issues found:**
- Experimental setup lacks detail on dataset split (train/val/test ratios not stated)
- Baseline comparison uses only one competing method — insufficient for peer review
- No mention of hardware/compute environment used

**Suggestions:**
- State dataset splits explicitly (e.g. 80/10/10) in the Methodology
- Add at least 2 more baseline methods for comparison (e.g. unstructured pruning, quantization)
- Include compute environment details (GPU type, training time, batch size)

---

### 4. Logical Consistency &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `12 / 15`

**Issues found:**
- Claim in Section 2 ("pruning preserves all semantic knowledge") contradicts results showing 1% accuracy drop
- Conclusion overstates findings — "state-of-the-art performance" not supported by the data

**Suggestions:**
- Soften the claim in Section 2 to "pruning largely preserves performance" to match experimental results
- Revise the conclusion to accurately reflect the scope of results (CIFAR-10 only, not generalised)

---

### 5. Readability Score &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `8 / 10`

**Issues found:**
- Average sentence length is 28 words — above the recommended 20 for technical writing
- 3 undefined acronyms used before being introduced (DNN, BN, FLOPs)

**Suggestions:**
- Aim to keep average sentence length under 22 words; split complex sentences
- Define all acronyms on first use — e.g. "Deep Neural Network (DNN)"

---

### 6. Abstract Quality &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `8 / 10`

**Issues found:**
- Abstract does not state the specific dataset used
- No quantitative result mentioned in Abstract (readers cannot judge contribution without opening the paper)

**Suggestions:**
- Add one sentence stating the dataset: "We evaluate on CIFAR-10..."
- Include the key quantitative result in the Abstract: "achieving 40% compression with <1% accuracy loss"

---

### 7. Conclusion Completeness &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `7 / 10`

**Issues found:**
- No future work direction mentioned
- Limitations of the approach are not acknowledged

**Suggestions:**
- Add a 2–3 sentence "Future Work" note (e.g. extending to ImageNet, exploring dynamic pruning)
- Acknowledge key limitation: results are on a small benchmark and may not generalise

---

### 8. Citation Quality &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; `6 / 10`

**Total citations found:** 14 &nbsp;&nbsp; | &nbsp;&nbsp; **DOIs extracted:** 9 &nbsp;&nbsp; | &nbsp;&nbsp; **Verified via CrossRef:** 7

**Flagged / Unverified DOIs:**
- `10.1145/9999.888888` — Not found in CrossRef (possible typo or retracted paper)
- `10.0000/fake.doi.001` — Invalid DOI format

**Suggestion:**
- Verify the 2 flagged DOIs manually and correct or remove them before submission

---

## Citations Verified: 7 / 9 DOIs confirmed &nbsp; ⚠ 2 flagged

---

## Overall Verdict

This paper presents a competent investigation into neural network compression with clear results.
The core methodology is sound, but the manuscript would benefit from a more detailed experimental setup,
stronger baseline comparisons, and tighter alignment between claims and findings.
Grammar and readability are generally acceptable with minor fixes required.

> **Recommendation: Needs minor revision before submission.**
> Address the flagged methodology gaps and citation issues, then resubmit for review.

## Design Decisions Captured (for Person 3 / Phase 4)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Header style | Minimal professional — title, filename, date only |
| Score display | Weighted per-parameter breakdown (marks out of unequal max per parameter) |
| Per-parameter content | Mark earned + issues found + specific improvement suggestions |
| Citations display | Summary line + flagged/unverified DOIs only (not the full verified list) |
| Verdict | Short summary paragraph (2–3 sentences) + clear recommendation line |

### Parameter Weights (from scoring.py — MUST match report exactly)

| Parameter | Weight | Max Marks in Report |
|---|---|---|
| Grammar & Language | 15% | 15 |
| Structural Integrity | 15% | 15 |
| Methodology Soundness | 15% | 15 |
| Logical Consistency | 15% | 15 |
| Readability Score | 10% | 10 |
| Abstract Quality | 10% | 10 |
| Conclusion Completeness | 10% | 10 |
| Citation Quality | 10% | 10 |
| **Total** | **100%** | **100** |

### ReportLab Implementation Notes

- **Library approach:** `PLATYPUS` (high-level flowable API) — NOT the low-level Canvas
  - Use `SimpleDocTemplate` as the document container
  - Build content as a list of flowable objects: `Paragraph`, `Table`, `Spacer`, `ListFlowable`, `HRFlowable`
  - PLATYPUS handles automatic page breaks — critical since parameter content is variable length
- **Fonts:** Use `Helvetica` (body) and `Helvetica-Bold` (headings) — built into ReportLab, no external font needed
- **Colours:** Use a single accent colour for section headings (`#1a73e8` — matches frontend)
- **Page size:** A4
- **Margins:** 2cm all sides
- **Score block:** Use a `Table` with background fill — green (`#34a853`) for A, blue (`#1a73e8`) for B, amber (`#f9ab00`) for C, red (`#ea4335`) for D/F
- **Parameter sections:** Each parameter is a `Paragraph` heading followed by two `ListFlowable` blocks (Issues / Suggestions)
- **Page footer:** Page number + "Generated by ResearchSense" on every page
- **Output / delivery:** Write to an in-memory `io.BytesIO` buffer — **do NOT save to disk**
  - `main.py` returns a `StreamingResponse` with `media_type="application/pdf"`
  - FastAPI header: `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="{original_name}_report.pdf"`
  - Browser triggers an immediate download — no file stored on the server

## Discussion Notes (Full Q&A — 18 May 2026)

These are the exact questions asked and answers given when designing this report.
Kept here so the reasoning behind every decision is transparent to the whole team.

---

### Q1 — Report Cover / Header

**Question asked:**
> What should appear at the top of the PDF report?
> Options: (1) Minimal header — title, filename, date | (2) Branded header with logo and university name | (3) Score-first — huge score at the very top

**Answer:** Option 1 — minimal header (title, filename, date)

**Additional note from user:** *"but I want the report to look professional and presentable"*

**Decision locked:**
- Header = `ResearchSense Analysis Report` (title)
- Sub-line = paper filename + analysis date
- No logo, no university branding — clean and professional
- Visual professionalism is achieved through layout, fonts, and spacing — not clutter

---

### Q2 — Score Display

**Question asked:**
> How should the final confidence score be shown inside the report?
> Options: (1) Score + Grade + horizontal bar | (2) Score + Grade text only | (3) Coloured score box/badge

**Answer (user redirected):** User did not pick from the options — instead clarified they want a **list of all parameters with individual weighted marks**, not just a single total score display.

**User's exact words:** *"actually a list of parameters each with some marks for example for grammar some marks but not every parameter should have same marks as not each parameter is equally important"*

**Decision locked:**
- No single "headline score box" as the dominant element
- Show each of the 8 parameters as a separate row with its own marks earned out of its own maximum
- Marks are weighted — Grammar is /15 not /10 because it carries 15% weight
- The total (e.g. 76/100) still appears in a summary table at the top, but the breakdown is the main body of the report
- Weights come directly from `scoring.py → WEIGHTS` — the report must stay in sync with that dict

---

### Q3 — Per-parameter Content

**Question asked:**
> Under each parameter, what should appear besides the mark?
> Options: (1) Mark only | (2) Mark + 2–3 bullet issues | (3) Mark + issues + suggestions

**Answer:** Option 3 — mark + issues found + suggestions for improvement

**User's reasoning:** *"as it will be more useful"*

**Decision locked:**
- Every parameter section has three parts: **score line**, **issues found** (bulleted), **suggestions** (bulleted)
- Gemini's analysis output for each layer must include both issues and suggestions (not just scores) — this is a requirement for `gemini_analyzer.py` in Phase 2
- Suggestions should be specific and actionable, not vague ("improve grammar" is not acceptable)

---

### Q4 — Citations Section

**Question asked:**
> How should the citations/references check appear in the report?
> Options: (1) Summary line only | (2) Summary + full list of all DOIs with ✓/✗ | (3) Summary + flagged/unverified DOIs only

**Answer:** Option 3 — summary + flagged DOIs only

**Decision locked:**
- Show one summary line: `X DOIs found | Y verified via CrossRef | Z flagged`
- Only list DOIs that **failed** verification — verified DOIs are not shown individually
- Each flagged DOI shows: the DOI string + reason (not found / invalid format / possible retraction)
- Keeps the report concise — a paper with 20 good citations shouldn't have a 20-row table

---

### Q5 — Final Verdict Section

**Question asked:**
> Should the report end with an overall written verdict?
> Options: (1) No verdict — numbers speak for themselves | (2) One-paragraph AI summary | (3) Short summary paragraph + clear recommendation line

**Answer:** Option 3 — short summary + recommendation line

**User's constraint:** *"but the summary should be short"*

**Decision locked:**
- Verdict = **2–3 sentences maximum** (not a full paragraph)
- Must mention: overall quality, 1–2 strongest weaknesses, and general direction
- Ends with a single **recommendation line** — one of:
  - `"This paper is ready for submission."`
  - `"This paper needs minor revision before submission."`
  - `"This paper needs major revision before submission."`
  - `"This paper is not suitable for submission in its current form."`
- Recommendation is determined by grade: A → ready, B → minor revision, C → major revision, D/F → not suitable
- This verdict is generated by Gemini as part of the analysis — NOT hardcoded rule strings

---

### Summary of All Decisions (one-line version)

| # | Topic | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Header | Minimal: title + filename + date. Professional look via layout, not logos. |
| 2 | Score | 8-parameter weighted breakdown (unequal max marks). Total shown in summary table. |
| 3 | Per-parameter | Mark + bulleted issues + bulleted suggestions. Both required from Gemini. |
| 4 | Citations | Summary line + flagged/unverified DOIs only. No full list of good citations. |
| 5 | Verdict | 2–3 sentence summary + one recommendation line. Grade determines recommendation. |
| 6 | PDF generation | ReportLab PLATYPUS. Direct download via BytesIO stream. No server storage. |

---

### Q6 — PDF Generation Library & Delivery

**Question asked:**
> Which ReportLab approach should be used, and where should the generated PDF be saved?
> Library options: (A) PLATYPUS high-level flowable API | (B) Canvas low-level manual drawing
> Delivery options: (1) Direct download, no server storage | (2) Saved to reports/ folder | (3) Both — saved then deleted after 5 min

**Answer:** PLATYPUS + Option 1 (direct download)

**Decision locked:**
- **Library:** ReportLab PLATYPUS (`SimpleDocTemplate` + flowable objects)
  - `Paragraph`, `Table`, `Spacer`, `ListFlowable`, `HRFlowable` are the building blocks
  - PLATYPUS was chosen because it handles automatic page breaks — essential since parameter sections vary in length depending on how many issues Gemini finds
  - Canvas was rejected — too low-level, requires manual X/Y positioning, breaks when content overflows a page
- **Delivery:** In-memory `io.BytesIO` buffer — PDF is never written to disk
  - `report_generator.py` writes to `BytesIO`, returns the buffer
  - `main.py` wraps it in a `StreamingResponse` with `media_type="application/pdf"`
  - FastAPI sets `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="{original_name}_report.pdf"` so browser downloads it immediately
  - No cleanup needed — nothing stored on server
- **Impact on main.py:** The `/analyze` endpoint in Phase 4 will return `StreamingResponse` instead of JSON when report generation is complete. This is a Phase 4 change — do not touch `main.py` until then.
- **`report_generator.py` signature** (final, replacing the current stub):
  ```python
  def generate_pdf_report(
      filename: str,
      sections: dict,
      layer_scores: dict,
      score_result: dict,
      citation_result: dict
  ) -> io.BytesIO:
      """Build and return a PDF report as an in-memory BytesIO buffer."""
  ```
